I farm the way I know best: I keep my land split between the wheat-maize rotation that gives my household steady grain and a smaller cotton area for cash income. I have 40 years in the field, and at my age I will not chase anything complicated or risky. Because I have well irrigation, I will use it to protect the key growth stages instead of depending only on rain. I will put most of my land into wheat followed by maize on the same fields, because that is the system I know and it fits my place in Quzhou County. I will keep a smaller cotton block because it still brings in money, but I will not expand it because it needs more labor and pest control. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stand establishment. For fertilizer, I will stay in a moderate range: enough nitrogen for yield, with phosphorus and potassium added so the soil does not get exhausted. I will use rotary tillage on most fields because it is practical for me, and I will keep pesticide sprays to the level needed to avoid major losses rather than spraying too often.
